triage.formula: urgency = (100 - score) + rateWeight x max(0, previousScore - score) / daysBetweenDraws. Order: RED (any red-flag value not explained by a sample problem) first, then AMBER (urgency >= amberUrgency or a value outside the lab range and away from the personal baseline), then GREEN.

cards.whoDecides: No action needed. Ground will see this at the next sync.

corpus.title: Glucose low
corpus.text: Blood sugar below 70 mg/dL is considered low.
steps: If it is still low, or you feel shaky, sweaty or confused, follow the 15-15 rule: 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate, then re-check after 15 minutes.
Repeat until you are back in range, then eat a snack with protein and carbohydrate.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer.

sources.label: CDC: Treatment of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)

corpus.title: Potassium low
corpus.text: Potassium is important to heart and muscle function.
steps: Tell your Crew Medical Officer today.
Write down any symptoms you notice in your log.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: Potassium blood test

corpus.title: Potassium high
corpus.text: Potassium is important to heart function. A damaged (hemolyzed) sample can falsely raise potassium.
steps: Ask for a new sample if the draw was difficult: a damaged sample can falsely raise potassium.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer today.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: Potassium test
UHNM Pathology: Common problems affecting blood test results

corpus.title: Sodium low
corpus.text: Low sodium can cause weakness, fatigue and confusion.
steps: Report weakness, fatigue or confusion right away.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: Sodium blood test

corpus.title: Sodium high
corpus.text: High sodium can be a sign of dehydration.
steps: Review your fluid intake with your Crew Medical Officer.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: Sodium blood test

corpus.title: Urea nitrogen bun high
corpus.text: Urea nitrogen is a waste product filtered by the kidneys; a high value can reflect dehydration.
steps: Review your fluid intake with your Crew Medical Officer.
Repeat at the next scheduled draw.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: BUN (blood urea nitrogen)

corpus.title: Ast high
corpus.text: AST is found in the liver and also in muscle; heavy muscle use can raise it.
steps: Log any intense exercise in the 24 hours before the draw.
Repeat at the next scheduled draw; tell your Crew Medical Officer if it stays high.

sources.label: MedlinePlus: AST test
Mayo Clinic content via Altru: AST blood test

corpus.title: Sample problem
corpus.text: When blood waits too long before the serum is separated, glucose falls and potassium rises inside the tube.
steps: Do not act on this value alone. Repeat the measurement with a fresh sample.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer that several crew members show the same change.

sources.label: NCI Biospecimen Research Database: delayed processing and serum glucose and potassium

corpus.title: Nausea, dizziness or disorientation in the first days of flight
corpus.text: Space motion sickness is common. A NASA technical report notes that nearly 70% of astronauts and cosmonauts are affected to some degree during their first several days of flight.
steps: Limit head movements and rest if your schedule allows.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer, especially if it is severe, starts after the first days of flight or does not get better.
Any anti-nausea medicine is decided by your Crew Medical Officer with the flight surgeon, not by this app.

sources.label: NASA NTRS 20040089364: Space adaptation syndrome, multiple etiological factors and individual differences
Smithsonian Air & Space: Sick in Space

corpus.title: Headache, congestion or slow thinking: check cabin CO2
corpus.text: On the ISS, crew reports of headache and congestion have been associated with cabin CO2 levels, and crews have reported symptoms below the spacecraft maximum allowable concentration. Since 2010, ISS operations have kept the 24-hour average CO2 at or below 4.0 mmHg. Air does not mix by convection in microgravity, so CO2 near you can be higher than a fixed sensor shows.
steps: Check the latest cabin CO2 reading in Space Health or on the station display.
Tell your Crew Medical Officer and report it to the ground: they decide whether CO2 removal or the work plan should change.
Note when the headache started and what you were doing; it helps the flight surgeon.

sources.label: NASA NTRS 20160012725: Relationship between CO2 levels and reported congestion and headaches on the ISS
NASA NTRS 20150019624: CO2 on the International Space Station, an operations update
NASA OCHMO Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004: Carbon Dioxide

corpus.title: A change in your vision (blurring, trouble focusing)
corpus.text: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) is a condition of long-duration spaceflight. A NASA clinical update reports that about 69% of long-duration astronauts show its earliest signs. It is tracked with scheduled eye exams.
steps: Report any new change in your vision to your Crew Medical Officer the same day.
Keep doing the scheduled eye exams; they are how SANS is tracked.

sources.label: NASA NTRS 20220000516: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), clinical update
NASA: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome

corpus.title: What the vital-signs score means
corpus.text: Space Health scores the vital signs it receives with the NEWS2 bands of the Royal College of Physicians: each value earns 0 to 3 points, and a total of 5 or more, or 3 points in one value, asks for an urgent review. NEWS2 was validated in hospitals on Earth, not in space, and our devices do not measure consciousness or oxygen therapy, so the score is partial.
steps: If your score is 5 or more, or one value is far out of range, tell your Crew Medical Officer now.
Repeat the measurement if you think the sensor slipped.

sources.label: Royal College of Physicians: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2

corpus.title: What Act now, Attention and Logged mean
corpus.text: Act now means a value is past a red-flag limit: call your Crew Medical Officer now. Attention means a value is outside the lab range and away from your own normal: repeat the test and review it. Logged means nothing to do now; it is checked at the next scheduled draw.

sources.label: Space Health rules engine (backend/clinical_rules.py, backend/switch_config.json)

corpus.title: Why my result is compared with my own pre-flight values
corpus.text: Space Health compares each value with the lab range and with the average of your own pre-flight draws. A value outside the lab range but within your usual band (for most tests 10%, tighter for sodium, chloride, calcium and potassium) is marked as your normal. A value that moved more than 25% from your average is marked as shifted even inside the lab range.

sources.label: Space Health rules engine (backend/clinical_rules.py, backend/switch_config.json)

corpus.title: Why several crew members got a 'possible sample problem' notice
corpus.text: When at least 3 crew members show the same change in the same draw, a handling or storage problem with the samples is more likely than the same illness in everyone. Space Health then shows one notice and asks for a repeat draw instead of several alarms.
steps: Repeat the draw when your Crew Medical Officer schedules it.

sources.label: Space Health rules engine (backend/clinical_rules.py, backend/switch_config.json)

corpus.title: Who decides what to do
corpus.text: The app never decides treatment. For Act now cards, your Crew Medical Officer acts on board without waiting for Earth. Other cards go to the flight surgeon on Earth, who confirms them or sends a directive; that reply arrives after the light delay of the link.

sources.label: Space Health rules engine (backend/clinical_rules.py, backend/switch_config.json)

corpus.title: What a trend watch means
corpus.text: When at least 3 in-mission draws of one test fall on a fairly straight line (R2 at least 0.6) and that line would leave the lab range within 30 days, the test goes on a watch list. A line through a few points is not a forecast; it only means: repeat the test sooner.
steps: Ask your Crew Medical Officer whether to move the next draw earlier.

sources.label: Space Health rules engine (backend/clinical_rules.py, backend/switch_config.json)
